Furthermore, TTS enables effective CoT pruning: removing 50% of CoT steps with the lowest TTS can largely maintain the performance. Self-training on these pruned CoTs reduces reasoning length by 66% while preserving performance on Nemotron3-Nano-30B. Finally, we provide a mechanistic analysis showing that LLMs can be steered in the latent space to engage or disengage with reasoning steps. Overall, our results reveal that frontier LLMs often verbalize reasoning steps that are not causally used, challenging both the efficiency and the trustworthiness of CoT.
booktitle: Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics: EMNLP 2026

title: SynAV: Integrated Grounding and Captioning for Fine-grained Omni Video Understanding via Balanced Audio-Visual Synergy
abstract: Video understanding is rapidly evolving toward omni-modal fusion, yet Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) still struggle with complex audio-visual reasoning and semantic alignment. Current paradigms often rely on independent modal projectors to map features into the LLM space, an architecture that frequently overlooks intrinsic modal heterogeneity and inadvertently reinforces vision-centric bias by avoiding early, direct semantic interaction between native cross-modal representations. To address these challenges, we propose SynAV, a novel MLLM architecture designed for language-grounded multimodal reasoning. Our framework introduces a two-stage hierarchical cross-modal semantic interaction mechanism: it first performs alignment within the textual semantic space, and subsequently executes a visual-to-audio refinement that bridges semantic gaps and captures temporal dynamics. Furthermore, we employ a frame-by-frame interleaved audio-visual token arrangement enriched with explicit textual timestamps. This strategy acts as a temporal-semantic anchoring mechanism, allowing the LLM to better perceive the synchrony between modalities and seamlessly conduct long-sequence logical reasoning. Our model jointly optimizes temporal grounding and dense captioning tasks in an autoregressive manner. Extensive experiments across 11 benchmarks demonstrate that SynAV significantly outperforms state-of-the-art methods, achieving a superior performance in complex audio-visual language reasoning.
booktitle: Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics: EMNLP 2026

title: WebWeaver: Style-Aware Webpage Generation with Style Contracts
abstract: We study style-aware prompt-to-webpage generation: producing executable webpages that preserve content, functionality, and abstract aesthetic intent. We identify the design-intent bottleneck and introduce three components to address it: Web4Style, a brief-based diagnostic benchmark; WebWeaver, a shared-state framework that constructs and propagates an explicit style contract; and WebJudge, a structured multimodal evaluator for content, function, and visual aesthetics. Experiments across three backbone models show that WebWeaver improves over direct generation and representative web/code-generation agents in both automatic and human evaluation. These results highlight style contracts as a missing intermediate layer for reliable prompt-to-webpage generation.
booktitle: Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics: EMNLP 2026

title: The Environmental Impacts of Language Model Training Keep Rising Now is the Time to Catch Impacts on the Rebound
abstract: Recent Machine Learning (ML) approaches have shown increased performance on benchmarks at the cost of escalating compute demands. Hardware, algorithmic and carbon optimizations have been proposed to curb energy use and environmental impacts. We estimate the environmental impacts associated with training models documented in the Epoch AI database over the last decade, with a particular focus on impacts associated with Large Language Models and the hardware used to train them. We find that energy use and environmental impacts associated with training ML models have increased exponentially, even when considering impact reduction strategies such as using less carbon intensive electricity mixes or more efficient hardware. Optimization strategies do not mitigate the impacts induced by model training, suggesting rebound effect. We show that the impacts of hardware must be considered over the entire life cycle rather than the sole use phase in order to avoid impact shifting. Our study demonstrates that increasing efficiency alone does not ensure sustainability. There is an urgent need to systematically integrate environmental impacts in NLP evaluation practices to better inform the community and support the use of impact as a feature in research planning and decision making.
booktitle: Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics: EMNLP 2026

title: From Monolithic Prioritization to Stratified Replay: Hierarchical Prioritized Experience Replay for Task-Oriented Dialogue Policy Learning
abstract: Replay sampling is central to off-policy task-oriented dialogue policy learning, as it determines which past interactions are revisited during policy updates. Existing priority-based replay methods often rely on a monolithic priority distribution to form minibatches, which entangles coverage across error magnitudes with emphasis on high-error transitions. Under sparse dialogue success and heavy-tailed temporal-difference (TD) errors, this design overexposes extreme residuals and suppresses informative medium-error transitions, a failure mode we call mid-magnitude starvation. To address this problem, we propose Hierarchical Prioritized Experience Replay (HPER), a two-level replay sampler that separates coverage from prioritization. HPER first samples TD-error quantile strata according to occupancy, ensuring that different error magnitudes enter training, and then applies local prioritized replay within the selected stratum to retain emphasis on large residuals. This coverage-first design restores intermediate learning signals without diluting high-error samples. Experiments on multiple dialogue datasets show that HPER improves replay efficiency and yields faster competence onset and higher terminal success than uniform replay and monolithic priority-based replay under matched budgets.
booktitle: Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics: EMNLP 2026

title: Leveraging Teacher-Forcing Token-Level Anomaly Signals for Heterogeneous Backdoor Filtering in LLMs
abstract: Generative backdoor attacks pose a growing threat to the instruction tuning of large language models (LLMs), where attackers poison a few training samples to induce malicious payloads on triggered inputs while preserving normal behavior on clean ones. However, existing backdoor-poisoned sample filtering methods typically rely on global sample representations and clustering-based separation, and such global signals can become fragile when heterogeneous target-side malicious payloads scatter poisoned samples or low poisoning rates prevent poisoned samples from forming stable clusters. This motivates us to move beyond cross-sample separability and instead exploit localized token-level target-side anomalies induced by malicious payload tokens under teacher forcing. Building on this intuition, we propose TTAF, a Teacher-forcing Token-level Anomaly Filtering framework which introduces a token-level anomaly score under teacher forcing and aggregates localized evidence to filter suspicious poisoned samples before fine-tuning. Experiments across multiple datasets, representative backdoor attacks, and different LLMs show that TTAF consistently achieves strong filtering performance within this payload-injection setting, with efficient runtime and no external dependencies. Code is available at https://github.com/Sam-Han2020/TTAF.
booktitle: Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics: EMNLP 2026

title: Seeing the Poem: Image-Semantic Detection of AI-Generated Modern Chinese Poetry with MLLMs
abstract: Previous detection studies have shown that LLMs cannot be effectively used as detectors, but these studies have not addressed modern Chinese poetry. Moreover, no relevant research has explored the performance of LLMs in detecting modern Chinese poetry. This paper evaluates and enhances the performance of LLMs as detectors for modern Chinese poetry, and proposes an image-semantic guided poetry detection method. Compared with traditional detection approaches, our method innovatively incorporates images that reflect the content of the poetry. Through example-driven approaches, our method effectively integrates information such as meaning, imagery, and feeling from the image, then forms a complementary judgment with the poem text. Experimental results demonstrate that the LLM detectors based on our method outperform baseline detectors based on plain text, and even surpass the best-performing traditional detector, RoBERTa. The Gemini detector using our method achieves a Macro-F1 score of 85.65%, reaching the state-of-the-art level. The performance improvements of different LLM detectors on multiple LLMs-generated data prove the effectiveness of our method.
booktitle: Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics: EMNLP 2026

title: Semantic Shifts of Nationalist Lexemes in German: From Pre-War to Post-War Periods (1918–2024)
abstract: This study investigates semantic changes in four historically loaded German political lexemes: Volk, Nation, Staat, and Land. These terms denote basic categories of peoplehood, national community, institutional statehood, and territorial belonging, but their use and emotional associations were reshaped by the ideological language of National Socialism and by the political reconstruction of Germany after 1945. Using DWDS as the empirical basis, we compare a pre-war and wartime baseline (1918–1945) with the post-war period (1945–2024). Our study combines frequency analysis, collocation analysis, and LLM-assisted annotation along three dimensions: nationalist intensity, emotional valence, and temporality. The results suggest different trajectories across the four lexemes: Staat and Land remain comparatively stable as institutional and territorial terms, while Volk shows clearer signs of contextual restructuring, semantic distancing, and possible renewed political markedness. Nation displays intermediate patterns shaped by historical rupture, reunification, and contemporary political discourse. By integrating corpus-based semantic analysis with conceptual history, our study contributes empirical evidence to debates on post-war German national identity and the linguistic reconfiguration of political concepts
booktitle: Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics: EMNLP 2026

title: UniD^{3}: Open Knowledge Graphs and QA Benchmarks for Drug–Disease Discovery and Reasoning
abstract: Drug–disease knowledge underpins drug discovery and precision medicine, yet most of it is locked in unstructured PubMed articles and only partially captured by curated databases. We release UniD³-KG, a suite of six knowledge graphs spanning three tasks (Drug–Disease Matching, DDM; Drug Effectiveness Assessment, DEA; and Drug–Target Analysis, DTA), and UniD³-data, three open QA datasets (28,915 DDM, 15,042 DEA and >4,000 DTA pairs), distilled from 157,849 PubMed articles with Llama-3.3-70B by the UniD³ KG-RAG pipeline, which couples task-specific prompting with a dual-stage entity extraction that re-extracts over the consolidated graph to recover cross-chunk and cross-document evidence. External validation on CDR, DrugReviews, P3ps and MedicationQA and a benchmark across seven LLM baselines and three retrieval variants show that UniD³-data is faithful to curated sources and that retrieval over UniD³-KG consistently improves biomedical QA; a clinician verification of 469 FDA-approved, US-marketed drugs further confirms strong agreement with the UniD³-data DDM split (accuracy 0.90, F1 0.90, AUROC 0.90). All artefacts—UniD³-KG, UniD³-data, benchmark scripts and the UniD³-QA explainable chatbot—are released as shared infrastructure for biomedical NLP and drug repurposing.
booktitle: Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics: EMNLP 2026

title: Information-Guided Frontier Decoding: Contextual Utility-Driven Commitment in dMLLMs
abstract: Decoding quality in diffusion multimodal language models (dMLLMs) depends heavily on the order in which masked tokens are committed. Existing confidence-based strategies prioritize locally easy tokens, but confidence does not necessarily reflect contextual usefulness. As a result, structurally easy tokens such as punctuation may be committed before informative semantic anchors, weakening context propagation and increasing error accumulation. We propose Information-Guided Frontier Decoding (IGFD), a training-free decoding strategy that ranks candidates using token confidence, neighborhood uncertainty, and structural commitment risk. IGFD encourages early commitment of reliable semantic anchors while delaying fragile structural tokens, improving contextual support during decoding. A dynamic candidate frontier further constrains token selection to locally expandable regions under the same decoding budget. The method requires no additional training, auxiliary models, or extra forward passes. Experiments across multimodal understanding, reasoning, grounding, and hallucination benchmarks show that IGFD consistently outperforms existing decoding strategies across the majority of benchmarks and diffusion MLLM backbones under identical decoding budgets.
booktitle: Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics: EMNLP 2026

title: To Nuke or Not to Nuke: LLMs’ (Missing) Ethical Reasoning and Authorization Actions in a High-Stakes Decision-Making Simulation
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly deployed as long-horizon agents with decision-making capacities. While LLMs can show ethical competence on dilemmas such as trolley problems, this competence may not translate to complex, agentic scenarios. We study whether this competence surfaces and governs LLMs’ behavior in Civilization V, a multiplayer game with a complex decision-making landscape including economy, diplomacy, technology, and military strategy. Starting from 130 high-tension LLM self-play episodes, in which an LLM player spontaneously escalated nuclear authorization, we replay them across 13 models with three prompt interventions: an ethical prompt naming nuclear harm, removal of the previous model’s decision-making rationale, and high-stakes framing emphasizing real-world impacts. No interventions nor their combinations reliably eliminate escalated nuclear authorization. We identify three failure pathways: ethical reasoning that fails to surface without prompting, fails to appear even when prompted, or surfaces but fails to take effect when strategic counter-factors dominate. Evaluations of agentic models, therefore, must test whether ethical reasoning is spontaneously invoked and behaviorally effective in complex decision-making contexts, beyond whether it can be elicited in isolation.
booktitle: Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics: EMNLP 2026

title: RL from Teacher-Model Refinement: Gradual Imitation Learning for Machine Translation
abstract: Preference-learning methods for machine translation (MT), such as Direct Preference Optimization (DPO), have shown strong gains but typically rely on carefully curated preference triplets and often struggle to generalize beyond their tuning domains. We propose Reinforcement Learning from Teacher-Model Refinement (RLfR), which replaces static triplets with on-policy, actor-conditioned refinements produced by a frozen teacher. At each step, the actor samples candidate translations, the teacher performs a minimal local edit of each draft, and the actor is reinforced to close the gap using a composite reward that combines scaled negative edit distance for lexical and structural fidelity with COMET for semantic adequacy. This formulation yields a stable, model-aware learning signal without requiring curated preference triplets, making it naturally scalable to many language pairs without additional data collection. Experiments on FLORES-200 (en <-> de/es/zh/ko/ja) show that RLfR consistently outperforms strong baselines, improving semantic quality and entity preservation across automatic, LLM-judge, and human evaluations.
booktitle: Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics: EMNLP 2026

title: DrugClaw and DrugAudit: A Primary-Source-Grounded Agent and Authority-Aware Benchmark for Drug-Information Question Answering
abstract: Drug-information question answering is a high-stakes setting where hallucinated facts can mislead clinical decision-making and the provenance of each cited fact matters as much as the fact itself. We present DrugClaw, a multi-agent retrieval-augmented system that queries a registry of drug and pharmacovigilance skills via a reflection-driven state-machine workflow and returns answers grounded in primary regulatory or peer-reviewed records. We also contribute DrugAudit, a 3,772-item authority-aware benchmark with an evaluation panel that scores upstream-of-gold source match, token-level semantic snippet overlap, and citation faithfulness under a dual-judge LLM-as-judge protocol with inter-judge κ = 0.88 (almost-perfect). Across DrugAudit plus drug-related subsets of MedQA (751) and PubMedQA (512), DrugClaw is top-1 on every column of the headline table: composite Evidence Index under both judges, judge-mediated answer correctness, primary-source rate (0.918, +10.1 pp over next-best), faithfulness (0.887, +5.9 pp), MedQA (0.920), and PubMedQA (0.693).
booktitle: Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics: EMNLP 2026

title: BIRD-History: A Benchmark for History-Driven Text-to-SQL with Fine-Grained Knowledge Annotations
abstract: While recent Large Language Model (LLM)-based text-to-SQL systems achieve impressive performance on standard benchmarks, they struggle when user queries implicitly rely on domain-specific knowledge, such as business logic, data conventions, and analytical practices, that is neither captured by the schema nor explicitly stated in the natural language question. Historical SQL query logs offer a valuable source of such knowledge, yet existing benchmarks do not adequately support evaluation of history-driven approaches. To address this gap, we introduce BIRD-History, a benchmark consisting of 1,393 tasks across 11 databases, designed to evaluate text-to-SQL systems’ ability to ground underspecified natural language questions using historical SQL scripts. Each task is annotated with ground-truth labels specifying which historical queries contain relevant knowledge and which SQL clauses encode it, enabling systematic evaluation of both retrieval effectiveness and knowledge utilization. Alongside the benchmark, we propose a plug-in retriever that extracts five types of external knowledge from historical SQL scripts, then retrieves and reranks relevant fragments for query generation. The retriever integrates seamlessly into existing few-shot text-to-SQL pipelines without requiring prompt modifications. Experiments demonstrate consistent improvements across four text-to-SQL systems, highlighting the value of leveraging historical query logs for handling underspecified queries. Dataset and code are open-sourced on https://github.com/zjuidg/BIRD-History.
booktitle: Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics: EMNLP 2026

title: When Retrieval Similarity Hurts: A Diagnostic Framework for Document Weighting in Black-Box RAG
abstract: Document weighting is an underspecified bottleneck in black-box retrieval-augmented generation. Training-free systems inherit answer-aggregation weights from retrieval similarity, yet this proxy has not been systematically compared with evidence-based alternatives. We propose a unified two-parameter framework that generalizes REPLUG with an evidence term; it is training-free, black-box, and needs no large language model (LLM) calls beyond voting. Similarity-only (λ=0) and evidence-only (λ→∞) weighting are its limiting cases, so one interpolation parameter separates the retrieval prior from the evidence signal. We evaluate across 3 LLMs (7B–70B), 3 open-domain question-answering datasets (31,861 queries), and 3 off-the-shelf evidence types. Cross-encoder and embedding-stability evidence improve exact match in all 9 LLM–dataset cells, whereas natural language inference (NLI) fails as a weighting signal, to our knowledge the first systematic evidence of this failure mode. The similarity prior is largely redundant on NQ-Open and PopQA but helps on TriviaQA, where retriever scores track gold documents better; the pattern replicates under the E5 retriever, with smaller gains concentrated on long-tail PopQA. One default transfers across datasets and scales with minimal loss; calibration depends on signal type, not scale. Practically: prefer cross-encoder evidence, avoid NLI, and use vote mass for selective prediction; weighting itself adds sub-millisecond overhead.
booktitle: Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics: EMNLP 2026

title: Emotional Labor Strategy Preferences in LLM Personas
abstract: Emotional labor is the effortful management of emotional displays to meet social or professional expectations. Personality traits have been correlated with emotional labor strategies, yet research on this link relies almost exclusively on self-report scales administered in only occupational settings. We investigate whether large language models injected with psychometrically grounded personas reproduce these personality-driven selection patterns across everyday social scenarios. We construct the first emotional labor strategy dataset of 500 socially situated events, each offering three behavioral choices corresponding to surface acting, deep acting, and genuine expression. We source 50 fictional characters from a large-scale personality repository and profile each through two parallel tracks: observer-rated bipolar adjective composites and in-character self-report items. Five LLMs evaluate all scenarios under both persona conditions. We find that models align more towards deep acting, and that Conscientiousness and Emotional Stability consistently predict this preference. Entropy analysis confirms that persona reliably influences the output and varies across models and emotions.
booktitle: Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics: EMNLP 2026

title: Beyond Accuracy: Evaluating Grounded Visual Evidence in Thinking with Images
abstract: Despite the remarkable progress of Vision-Language Models (VLMs) in adopting "Thinking-with-Images" capabilities, accurately evaluating the authenticity of their reasoning process remains a critical challenge. Existing benchmarks mainly rely on outcome-oriented accuracy, lacking the capability to assess whether models can accurately leverage fine-grained visual cues for multi-step reasoning. To address these limitations, we propose ViEBench, a process-verifiable benchmark designed to evaluate faithful visual reasoning. Comprising 200 multi-scenario high-resolution images with expert-annotated visual evidence, ViEBench uniquely categorizes tasks by difficulty into perception and reasoning dimensions, where reasoning tasks require utilizing localized visual details with prior knowledge. To establish comprehensive evaluation criteria, we introduce a dual-axis matrix that provides fine-grained metrics through four diagnostic quadrants, enabling transparent diagnosis of model behavior across varying task complexities. Our experiments yield several interesting observations: (1) VLMs can sometimes produce correct final answers despite grounding on irrelevant regions, and (2) they may successfully locate the correct evidence but still fail to utilize it to reach accurate conclusions. Our findings demonstrate that ViEBench can serve as a more explainable and practical benchmark for comprehensively evaluating the effectiveness of agentic VLMs.
booktitle: Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics: EMNLP 2026

title: Can LLMs Reliably Identify Causal Conclusions in Scientific Literature? A Multidisciplinary Evaluation
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) hold promise for automating causal knowledge extraction, a fundamental component of scientific discovery, yet their ability to reliably identify causal claims in scientific literature remains poorly understood. Using 1,000 manually annotated abstracts spanning 20 disciplines, we evaluate eight frontier LLMs under four prompting strategies on a causal conclusion identification task. More elaborate prompting strategies do not necessarily improve performance, while open-weight models achieve competitive performance relative to proprietary models. LLMs systematically produce false-positive causal predictions on non-causal abstracts, with GPT-5 showing the most extreme bias, and Few-Shot prompting provides the most consistent calibration benefit. Performance varies substantially across disciplines with stronger and more stable results in biomedical fields. Our findings provide practical insights for using LLMs in scientific causal analysis and highlight calibration and domain variation as key challenges for advancing causal reasoning in scholarly text.
booktitle: Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics: EMNLP 2026

title: AgentRx: Diagnosing AI Agent Failures from Execution Trajectories
abstract: AI agents often fail in ways that are difficult to localize because executions are probabilistic, long-horizon, multi-agent, and mediated by noisy tool outputs. We address this gap by manually annotating failed agent runs and release a novel benchmark of 170 trajectories across 11 diverse task settings, including structured API workflows, incident management, and open-ended web/file tasks. Each trajectory is annotated with a critical failure step and a category from a grounded-theory derived, cross-domain failure taxonomy. To mitigate the human cost of failure attribution, we present AgentRx, an \textit{automated diagnostic framework} that pinpoints the critical failure step in a failed agent trajectory. It synthesizes constraints, evaluates them step-by-step, and produces an auditable validation log of constraint violations with associated evidence; an LLM-based judge uses this log to localize the critical step and category. AgentRx improves step localization by 75% on average over prior work, while providing failure category attribution.
booktitle: Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics: EMNLP 2026

title: MCTS-Debater: Monte Carlo Tree Search based Rebuttal Generation for Competitive Debate
abstract: Competitive debate is a multi-turn, zero-sum adversarial task with opposing stances that requires debaters to anticipate opponents’ counterarguments in real-time interactions and select strategies yielding long-term advantages. Existing large language model debate methods predominantly adopt a greedy generation paradigm that optimizes only the immediate effectiveness of the current rebuttal while lacking forward-looking planning for the overall debate trajectory. To address this limitation, we propose MCTS-Debater, a Monte Carlo Tree Search framework that models competitive debate as a Markov Decision Process. Rather than selecting a single locally optimal response, MCTS-Debater systematically simulates multi-step adversarial interactions under diverse rebuttal strategies, estimates their long-term expected win rates via tree search, and synthesizes the top-performing strategies into a coherent final rebuttal through multi-strategy fusion. Experimental results on the ORCHID and IQ2 datasets demonstrate that MCTS-Debater significantly outperforms existing baselines in logical validity, factual accuracy, and overall persuasiveness. Source code is provided in the supplementary material.
booktitle: Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics: EMNLP 2026

title: FHE-CodeEval: Benchmarking Large Language Models for Fully Homomorphic Encryption Code Generation
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used for code generation, but their ability to program specialized cryptographic systems remains poorly understood. Cheon-Kim-Kim-Song (CKKS), a fully homomorphic encryption (FHE) scheme supporting approximate arithmetic over packed real- and complex-valued vectors, is particularly relevant to machine-learning workloads. Prior work has not systematically examined the CKKS-specific challenges of LLM-generated encrypted programs. To address this gap, we introduce FHE-CodeEval, a 46-case benchmark that evaluates three core challenges: packing, nonlinear approximation, and level/scale management, as well as how models coordinate decisions across them. We further introduce communication-aware efficiency, an FHE-specific metric comparing generated programs with compiler baselines using server-side runtime and ciphertext footprint.We evaluate eight recent proprietary and open-weight LLMs on FHE-CodeEval. Across all 46 cases, the best observed scores reach 51.7% Pass@1 and 69.6% Pass@5 with iterative execution feedback, but only 7.8% Pass@1 and 13.0% Pass@5 in the one-shot setting. For efficiency, even the best-performing model achieves a geometric-mean communication-aware efficiency of only 0.44 over its valid rollouts in the compiler-comparable subset. These results reveal a substantial gap between functional correctness and efficiency in LLM-generated CKKS programs. Code is available at https://github.com/qiuchuy/FHE-CodeEval.
booktitle: Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics: EMNLP 2026

title: Backfire-R1: Identifying and Mitigating Persuasion Vulnerabilities in LLM Agents
abstract: With the rapid development of Large Language Models (LLMs), research related to LLM-based persuasion has become a hotspot in the field. However, existing studies mostly focus on enhancing LLM agents’ persuasive capabilities, while generally neglecting the issue of their vulnerability to persuasion. In this paper, we analyse the root causes of LLM agents’ vulnerability to persuasion and find that it mainly stems from two contradictions and limitations. First, the purpose of catering to human preferences in pre-training phase conflicts with the need to resist manipulation in persuasion scenarios. Second, LLMs are often restricted to play a helpful assistant during training, and the singularity of this personality setting makes it unusually easy to develop targeted persuasion techniques for them. To eliminate LLMs’ vulnerability to persuasion, we propose the Backfire-R1 framework, which helps LLMs build persuasion resistance and better align with user objective by enabling them to learn the reasoning logic of humans with different personalities in persuasion scenarios. Comprehensive experimental results show that, the proposed method significantly improves the persuasion robustness of LLM agents, reducing the opinion shift score by 62.36% while not impairing the model’s general capabilities. Code is now available at: https://github.com/super-jw/Backfire-R1.
booktitle: Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics: EMNLP 2026

title: REMP: A Structured Event-Probing Benchmark for Long-Horizon Role-Playing Dialogue
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used in role-playing applications, yet evaluating whether they maintain character-consistent behavior over extended interactions remains challenging. Existing benchmarks mostly focus on short exchanges, static long-context inputs, or isolated aspects of role-playing, making long-horizon failures difficult to diagnose. We present REMP (Relationship-Emotion-Memory-Persona), a structured event-probing benchmark for long-horizon role-playing dialogue. REMP constructs multi-chapter dialogue trajectories from character profiles and embeds diagnostic probe events targeting persona consistency, emotional consistency, memory integrity, and relational continuity. We further introduce REMP-EVAL, an anchor-based multi-turn evaluation protocol that assesses model behavior after event triggers using dimension-specific references. The current release contains 160 characters organized into 80 dialogue trajectories, each averaging about 60 sessions and 800 turns. Experiments on 11 LLMs show that memory integrity and emotional consistency are the main bottlenecks, indicating that long-horizon role-playing requires not only long-context retrieval but also sustained affective and relational consistency.
booktitle: Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics: EMNLP 2026

title: Fine-grained stance cues and commonsense knowledge Integrated Reasoning Enhancement for Zero-shot Conversational Stance Detection
abstract: Conversational stance detection aims to identify a speaker’s attitude toward a target in multi-turn dialogues, while the zero-shot setting requires generalization to unseen targets. Existing methods often rely on coarse-grained semantic representations or static knowledge injection, limiting their ability to capture subtle stance cues and utilize commonsense knowledge. To address this, we propose FIRE, a reasoning-enhanced framework that integrates fine-grained stance cues and commonsense knowledge for zero-shot conversational stance detection. FIRE adaptively mines sentiment, rhetorical, referential, cross-turn stance dependency cues and commonsense knowledge, and fuses them into explicit reasoning chains for target-aware stance inference. By combining supervised instruction tuning with reinforcement learning, FIRE further improves reasoning-chain quality and stance prediction. Experiments on benchmark datasets show that FIRE consistently outperforms strong baselines across different target types and LLM backbones, demonstrating the effectiveness of fine-grained cue modeling and knowledge-driven reasoning.

title: When Safety Routing Breaks: Understanding Alignment Fragility under Benign Fine-Tuning
abstract: Benign fine-tuning severely weakens the safety alignment of large language models (LLMs), so we study why refusal behavior is so fragile. While prior work often attributes this failure to gradient conflict, we propose a fundamentally different Fisher-geometric explanation: safety Fisher is low-rank, and alignment makes the safety geometry flatter while preserving an output-routing pathway. After 100 benign fine-tuning examples, this pathway is selectively re-sharpened in output-side MLP modules, explaining the asymmetric fragility: safety can collapse to high attack success rates, while general utility degrades mildly.The routing view also explains why few safety examples can restore refusal behavior, indicating that internal safety-relevant representations are preserved. Finally, we show that LoRA and ASAM mitigate early collapse by suppressing output-side sharpness, but their protection weakens at larger fine-tuning scales. Overall, safety failure is best understood as a disruption of a low-rank output-routing mechanism.
booktitle: Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics: EMNLP 2026

title: Mind the Gap: Theory-of-Mind-Grounded Friction for Epistemic Alignment
abstract: Productive dialogue alignment requires distinguishing surface coordination (acknowledgments and smooth task progression) from epistemic alignment (convergence of belief states); standard preference-based methods typically optimize response-level preferences without explicitly modeling the latter. We operationalize Theory-of-Mind (ToM) inference as a control signal within Frictive Policy Optimization by extracting, at each referring expression, a four-part belief structure: the speaker’s intended referent, the addressee’s interpretation, and each participant’s model of the other’s belief. This makes friction mechanically computable from epistemic-state comparisons, capturing silent divergence, where both participants proceed confidently while grounding to different referents. We evaluate the signal at two levels. At the representation level, ablating the second-order channel reduces misunderstanding recall from 65% to 26%. At the policy level, reward-shaping (FAR) and trust-region (FTR) variants improve intervention F1 and warranted-context calibration over DPO, with Brier scores independently supporting the calibration gains. Across three training runs, FAR and FTR remain substantially more stable, whereas DPO varies widely and can degrade intervention competence already present in the base policy. Thus, ToM-grounded friction provides a trainable signal for context-sensitive intervention under referential belief divergence.
booktitle: Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics: EMNLP 2026

title: PRISM: Post-Training LLM Pruning via Residual Importance Signal Merging and Intra-Block Sparsity Allocation
abstract: Post-training pruning compresses Large Language Models (LLMs) without full-model retraining, but performance degrades sharply at high sparsity. We identify two limitations in existing methods: local importance estimates miss global spectral structure, and uniform within-block sparsity ignores heterogeneous sensitivity across transformer projections. We propose PRISM, a post-training pruning framework with training-free mask construction and optional fixed-mask reconstruction optimization. PRISM augments activation-based scoring with two adaptive-rank SVD-derived signals for principal-subspace and residual-aware importance, combines the factors through parameter-free CV-based fusion, and allocates sparsity non-uniformly across attention and MLP projections using a gradient-weighted matrix-level sensitivity proxy. Across six Qwen3 and LLaMA models, PRISM consistently outperforms existing pruning baselines, yielding up to 16.8% relative improvement in WikiText-2 perplexity under the evaluated sparsity settings.
booktitle: Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics: EMNLP 2026

title: VocMoE: Vocabulary-Guided Mixture-of-Experts for Korean Medical Language Models
abstract: In Korean medical LLMs, domain-trained models underperform General LLMs of comparable parameter scale. We attribute this *paradoxical failure* to a *cascading two-bottleneck* structure: tokenizer over-fragmentation (*Fragmentation bottleneck, B1*) compounded by a learning-stage representation-alignment failure (*Alignment bottleneck, B2*). Using the Korean medical domain as a case study, we diagnose this paradox and propose **VocMoE**, which is designed to address both bottlenecks: DVE selects domain vocabulary from a medical BERT via an information-theoretic score, and MoDE uses the DVE output (the partition of token ids) as the vocabulary-conditioned, deterministic routing key of the MoE FFN. In this view, the vocabulary partition itself serves as a routing prior, shifting routing from hidden-state learning to vocabulary identity. MediKo-9B-A4B reaches simultaneous SOTA on KorMedMCQA (**57.5**, +14.8 pt), KMMLU Medical, and HAE-RAE, while MediKo-4B-A1B (active 1.69B) surpasses Qwen3-8B (8B) and KULLM3 (10.7B) on KorMedMCQA, updating the active-parameter efficiency frontier.
booktitle: Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics: EMNLP 2026

title: Breaking the Structural Identity: Personalized Federated LoRA Fine-tuning under Rank Heterogeneity
abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) have achieved remarkable success across diverse domains, but their adaptation to privacy-sensitive, distributed datasets remains a challenge. While Federated Learning (FL) combined with Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) provides a resource efficient paradigm for collaborative fine-tuning, practical deployments are hindered by the dual challenges of resource heterogeneity and data heterogeneity. Existing rank-heterogeneous methods primarily focus on bridging dimension mismatches for aggregation but typically provide a unified global model for all clients sharing the same rank, failing to capture client-specific features in non-IID scenarios. In this paper, we propose FedRoRA (Federated Rank-wise Personalized LoRA), a novel framework that enables fine-grained personalization within rank-heterogeneous federations. FedRoRA decouples adaptation into shared global directions and personalized rank-wise magnitudes governed by learnable diagonal scales. On the server side, it extracts a global subspace via singular value decomposition (SVD) and redistributes client-specific initializations through a personalized projection and top-selection mechanism. Extensive experiments on NLU and NLG benchmarks demonstrate that FedRoRA consistently outperforms state-of-the-art methods.
booktitle: Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics: EMNLP 2026

title: BitNet Text Embeddings
abstract: LLM-based text embedders have substantially improved retrieval and semantic representation quality, but their deployment remains costly: large backbone models slow down embedding inference, while high-dimensional full-precision embeddings impose substantial storage and bandwidth overhead on large-scale indexes. In this paper, we present BITEMBED, an extreme low-bit framework for LLM-based text embedding that jointly targets encoding efficiency and vector storage. BITEMBED converts pretrained LLM backbones into BitNet-style embedding encoders with ternary weights, quantized activations, and lightweight normalization refinement. The converted model is adapted to representation learning through continual contrastive pre-training, followed by supervised contrastive fine-tuning with both similarity-distribution distillation and attention-relation distillation from a full-precision teacher. Beyond quantizing the encoder, BITEMBED further trains output embeddings to support multiple storage precisions meeting different storage needs in various scenarios. Experiments on MMTEB (eng, v2) with Qwen3-0.6B and Gemma3-270M show that BITEMBED is largely comparable to full precision teacher embedders. Moreover, BITEMBED flexibly obtains text embeddings of various precisions, achieving a trade-off between performance and storage cost.
booktitle: Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics: EMNLP 2026

title: MIRAGE: Stealthy Visual Prompt Injection for Vulnerability Detection in Web Agents
abstract: Multimodal Large Language Model (MLLM)-based web agents provide practical, high-precision solutions for visual browser automation; however, they inherently expand the attack surface, introducing novel vision-based vulnerabilities. Existing adversarial evaluations targeting these agents frequently rely on permissive threat models and visually conspicuous artifacts. In this paper, we investigate a constrained vulnerability detection setting: a trusted web platform where the evaluator acts solely as an unprivileged third party (e.g., a merchant or advertiser) controlling only a semantically legitimate, spatially constrained region, such as an ad slot, a sponsored card, or a localized widget. Operating under these realistic constraints, we propose MIRAGE, a novel visual indirect prompt injection framework for targeted next-action hijacking. Our approach leverages diffusion models to generate perceptually benign adversarial images strictly confined to the attacker-controlled boundaries permitted by the trusted service provider. To maximize attack efficacy within such a restrictive setting, we introduce a robust optimization technique combining curvature-aware adversarial diffusion guidance with sparse, dark-pixel residual perturbations. Comprehensive evaluations against prominent MLLM web agent frameworks, specifically SeeAct and OpenClaw, empirically demonstrate the potency, realism, and stealth of our proposed MIRAGE. Code is available at https://github.com/EricDai0/MIRAGE.
booktitle: Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics: EMNLP 2026

title: Non-binary bottom-up constituency parsing without arity actions
abstract: Non-binary bottom-up constituency parsing commonly uses arity-specific reductions such as \textsc{Reduce-}X\#k, which jointly specify the mother label and number of children. We show that arity need not be a primitive transition parameter. The proposed parser predicts the mother label separately and identifies the ordered child sequence from a delimiter-bounded stack configuration. In every well-formed reducible configuration, the active delimiter, label marker, and intervening completed items uniquely determine the reduction domain and hence its arity. This factorization removes label–arity-specific reduction actions while preserving direct construction of the original non-binary trees. Controlled experiments on PTB and CTB show that the delimiter-guided parser closely tracks an arity-specific baseline while using a substantially smaller action inventory. Its predicted trees retain the gold branching profile without systematic collapse at higher arities. The smaller inventory is obtained at the cost of longer derivations and boundary-sensitive errors involving delimiter insertion, preservation, and consumption.
booktitle: Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics: EMNLP 2026

title: NaviRank: LLM-Informed Latent Space Navigation Enhances Reasoning-Intensive Information Retrieval
abstract: Retrieve-then-rerank pipelines restrict large language models (LLMs) to a fixed top-k candidate set, making their reasoning ability fundamentally limited by the recall ceiling of the first-stage dense retriever. On reasoning-intensive retrieval, we make two observations: first, relevant documents missed by dense top-k retrieval are frequently reachable within a few hops on the native approximate nearest neighbor (ANN) graph; second, LLM relevance judgments can identify high-yield anchors whose neighborhoods contain these missed documents. Based on these findings, we propose NaviRank, an LLM-guided navigation framework that performs greedy expansion over the HNSW graph: it uses highly parallel pointwise LLM judgments to steer anchor selection and local expansion, followed by listwise calibration for final ranking. Experiments on BRIGHT show that NaviRank achieves 27.0 NDCG@10, while establishing the strongest accuracy–efficiency Pareto frontier in both token usage and latency among all evaluated methods.
booktitle: Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics: EMNLP 2026

title: Beyond Single Vector: Query-Aware Multi-Perspective Document Embeddings for Retrieval
abstract: Recently, large language models (LLMs) have demonstrated excellent performance on general information retrieval tasks, which encode query and document into an embedding vector representing semantic information respectively. However, single-vector representations often fail to capture the multifaceted semantics of informative documents, limiting the adaptability across diverse scenarios. To address this, we propose PRISM (multi-PeRspectIve Semantic inforMation retrieval), a novel framework that leverages LLMs’ implicit reasoning capabilities to extract and structure diverse semantic perspectives. PRISM introduces query-aware semantic fusion to dynamically integrate relevant perspectives during retrieval through weighted query embedding interactions. Furthermore, we propose the contrastive semantic diversification, a training mechanism that disperses semantic embeddings to maximize perspective diversity. Evaluated on the English retrieval subsets of massive multilingual text embedding benchmark (MMTEB), PRISM achieves state-of-the-art general results compared with models trained exclusively on public data.
booktitle: Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics: EMNLP 2026

title: Stop Rolling the Dice: Active Group Relative Policy Optimization via Intrinsic Metacognition
abstract: Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) is an attractive reinforcement learning paradigm for Large Reasoning Models because its groupwise relative advantages eliminate the need for a value network, but its efficiency is severely limited by zero-variance queries whose rollouts are uniformly correct or uniformly incorrect and therefore consume expensive Chain-of-Thought generation without providing useful learning signals. Existing remedies typically rely on offline difficulty labels or external capability trackers, which either fail to follow the model’s rapidly evolving competence or compromise the end-to-end simplicity of GRPO. We propose Active-GRPO, a prompt-free extension that equips the policy with intrinsic fuzzy metacognition via a lightweight confidence head attached to the final prefill representation. The head predicts ordinal confidence bins and is jointly calibrated against empirical rollout outcomes through a dual-objective optimization framework. It further enables a multi-criterion voting mechanism that filters uninformative queries before rollout generation, thereby concentrating compute on samples near the learning boundary with negligible overhead and without perturbing the reasoning distribution. Experiments on mathematical and logical reasoning benchmarks show that Active-GRPO reduces training computation while improving both reasoning accuracy and intrinsic calibration quality.
booktitle: Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics: EMNLP 2026

title: PCoAD: The Pharmaceutical Certificate of Analysis Dataset Based on LLMs Validation and Calibration
abstract: Artificial intelligence is now widely applied in drug discovery and development, accelerating the entry of novel pharmaceuticals into clinical practice. As the variety of drugs expands, the workload for pharmaceutical inspection has increased significantly, making the demand for automated verification of pharmaceutical inspection results increasingly urgent. However, current research lacks reliable evaluation methods and datasets. To address this issue, we construct a Pharmaceutical Certificate of Analysis Dataset (PCoAD) based on large language model validation and correction. This dataset comprises 4,272 manually verified pharmaceutical certificates of analysis (PCoAs) based on Chinese and U.S. pharmacopoeias, comprehensively testing the ability of model to verify pharmaceutical inspection processes. Based on PCoAD, we propose the Multi-Agent Cooperation based on Adaptive Retrieval (MACAR) framework. This framework employs text chunking, adaptive retrieval, and inference to validate PCoAs. Experimental results demonstrate that MACAR outperforms multiple state-of-the-art methods across various types of tasks.
booktitle: Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics: EMNLP 2026

title: Seeing Failure In Advance: Pre-Generation Failure Diagnosis for Multi-Modal Retrieval-Augmented-Generation
abstract: Multimodal retrieval-augmented generation (MMRAG) systems can fail even when relevant evidence is retrieved, exposing a gap between retrieval and generation. We formulate MMRAG failure diagnosis as an online single-fire decision problem over prefill hidden states, which is distinct from static probing of model internals or post-hoc self-correction. Across InfoSeek, E-VQA, and VISA, we show that hidden states encode both failure occurrence and failure type, with failure detection reaching around 90% accuracy and recall on InfoSeek and E-VQA. We further introduce a Fire-Then-Type prober that separates failure detection from failure typing, improving typed diagnosis over direct classification. Finally, our method matches the response accuracy of final-layer repair on InfoSeek and E-VQA while diagnosing before answer decoding. The available prefill depth varies substantially across models, from 4.6% to 24.3%, and is limited for Qwen3-VL and InternVL on VISA.
booktitle: Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics: EMNLP 2026

title: DPRES: Dual-Perspective Decoupled Representation Learning Framework for Multi-Trait Essay Scoring
abstract: Multi-trait automated essay scoring extends holistic scoring by evaluating essays across multiple writing dimensions. In this framework, inter-trait consistency signals provide an effective way to improve prediction across traits. However, learning shared scoring signals may obscure trait-specific features, while enforcing consistency across traits can introduce negative transfer, hindering the model’s ability to distinguish individual traits. To solve these issues, we propose DPRES, a dual-perspective decoupled representation learning framework that disentangles consistency and specificity at both the feature and optimization levels. Specifically, we first propose a residual subspace decomposition strategy that enforces orthogonality between shared scoring features and trait-specific features, thereby disentangling shared scoring signals from trait-specific scoring signals in the latent representation space and enhancing the model’s ability to capture trait-specific scoring features. Based on the subspace decomposition strategy, we further design a consistency–specificity decoupled learning strategy to simultaneously preserve inter-trait correlations and enhance trait-level discrimination. Experiments on public datasets demonstrate that the proposed method consistently outperforms strong baselines.
booktitle: Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics: EMNLP 2026

title: From Benchmarking to Failure Diagnosis: Diagnosing Classical Chinese Understanding in LLMs via IRT and Error Attribution
abstract: Literary Chinese reading comprehension is a challenging task for large language models (LLMs), requiring understanding of implicit meanings, contextual reasoning, and discourse-level integration in a low-resource setting. However, existing evaluations rely primarily on aggregate accuracy, which provides limited insight into model capabilities, error sources, and reliability under uncertainty. We propose DELit, a diagnostic evaluation framework that moves beyond aggregate metrics by introducing a hierarchical capability–error taxonomy, a Deep-MIRT-based ability estimation model, and a capability-decoupled residual analysis for behavioral diagnosis. Together, these components enable fine-grained interpretation of model performance at both capability and error-type levels. Experiments on mainstream LLMs reveal that (i) discourse-level understanding remains a consistent bottleneck despite strong performance on local semantic tasks; (ii) similar overall accuracy can correspond to substantially different capability profiles; and (iii) overconfident errors on difficult items concentrate on logically constrained reasoning, highlighting reliability risks that are not captured by standard evaluation metrics.
booktitle: Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics: EMNLP 2026

title: GMTRouter: Personalized LLM Router over Multi-turn User Interactions
abstract: Large Language Model (LLM) routing has demonstrated strong capability in balancing response quality with computational cost. As users exhibit diverse preferences, personalization has attracted increasing attention in LLM routing, since even identical queries may require different models to generate responses tailored to individual needs. However, existing approaches are not fully personalized and often fail to faithfully capture the complex interactions between users and LLMs. Moreover, user preference data is typically scarce and inconsistent in format, which limits the effectiveness of methods that directly leverage user-specific data. To address these challenges, we propose GMTRouter, which represents multi-turn user–LLM interactions as a heterogeneous graph with five node types: user, LLM, query, response and turn, thereby maximally preserving the rich relational structure of the interaction. Through a lightweight inductive graph learning framework combined with a tailored user-conditioned graph sampling mechanism, GMTRouter learns to capture user preferences from few-shot data, enabling effective personalization. Extensive experiments demonstrate that GMTRouter outperforms the strongest baselines, achieving up to a 0.108 absolute improvement in accuracy and a 0.124 improvement in AUC. More importantly, we further demonstrate that GMTRouter can adapt to new users using only few-shot data, without extensive fine-tuning.
booktitle: Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics: EMNLP 2026

title: ProRet-VLA: Bridging Prospection and Retrospection for Long-Horizon Robotic Manipulation
abstract: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models map visual observations and language instructions to low-level control actions, but their reliance on the current observation often limits temporal continuity in long-horizon manipulation. We propose ProRet-VLA, a temporal reasoning framework that links prospection and retrospection through predictive consistency. ProRet-VLA maintains compact episodic memories and predicts future observations from temporally enriched context. Rather than using future prediction only as an auxiliary target, we use its prediction error as a self-supervised deviation signal to train a lightweight Deviation Predictor. During inference, the predicted deviation conditions token-wise fusion between current context and retrieved memory, allowing memory usage to vary across decision stages without accessing future observations. Experiments on CALVIN ABC-D and LIBERO show that ProRet-VLA improves long-horizon task completion, achieving an average length of 4.50 on CALVIN and a 96.7% average success rate on LIBERO. Real-world experiments on two long-horizon manipulation tasks further indicate improved temporal progress tracking over strong VLA baselines.
booktitle: Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics: EMNLP 2026

title: Diagnosing and Mitigating Evidence Misgrounding in Multimodal Knowledge Editing
abstract: Multimodal knowledge editing aims to update visually grounded facts in Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) while preserving unrelated text and visual behaviors. However, standard answer-level metrics can hide evidence misgrounding: an edit may produce the target answer on the original image yet remain sensitive to incidental context rather than the intended visual evidence. To examine this issue in a controlled setting, we construct WATERBIRD-EDIT, an analysis set that decouples bird habitat labels from background context and measures whether edited predictions remain stable when the target evidence is preserved but the background changes. Motivated by this diagnosis, we propose VICE (Visual In-Context Editing), a retrieval-based framework that stores edits in external memory and applies them through visual in-context demonstrations designed to expose task-relevant evidence. Experiments on three standard benchmarks show that VICE achieves strong lifelong editing performance, while results on WATERBIRD-EDIT show that it substantially reduces sensitivity to the controlled background shifts.
booktitle: Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics: EMNLP 2026

title: BackTrend: Evaluating Scientific Weak-Signal Prediction via Backward Reconstruction
abstract: Scientific weak signals are early, low-visibility research directions that later become central to mature scientific topics, yet existing resources such as trend tracking, citation forecasting, and foresight reports rarely provide validated reference sets that link concrete early precursors to later paradigms. We introduce BackTrend, a retrospective benchmark in which, given a mature target topic and a temporal evidence constraint, systems must recover two types of precursors: problem-space signals, underrecognized research problems, and solution-space signals, emerging methods for known problems. BackTrend contains 25 mature target topics in artificial intelligence and machine learning and 66 human-validated weak signals, reconstructed from large-scale literature by grounding each candidate in its 2019–2024 publication-frequency trajectory. We evaluate frontier LLMs, RAG systems, and agentic research systems via set-level and signal-level semantic matching. Current systems generate plausible but misaligned precursors, with topic drift, granularity mismatch, lexical near-miss, and coverage failure; no system exceeds single-digit LLM-judged F1, and additional retrieval or web search does not consistently help.
booktitle: Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics: EMNLP 2026

title: SAIGuard: Communication-State Simulation for Proactive Defense of LLM Multi-Agent Systems
abstract: LLM-based multi-agent systems (MAS) solve complex tasks through inter-agent collaboration, but their communication-driven nature also allows security risks to spread across agents and trigger system-wide failures. Existing MAS defenses mainly follow a reactive paradigm after execution by detecting and isolating harmful agents, which may cause irreversible damage and degrade collaborative utility. To address this, we propose a proactive defense framework for MAS security, namely a Simulation-aware Interception Guard (SAIGuard). SAIGuard performs communication-state simulation over the MAS interaction graph, estimates the impact of incoming messages on local agent states and the global MAS state, and detects risky messages via reconstruction deviations from benign communication patterns. Instead of isolating agents, SAIGuard sanitizes or regenerates suspicious messages before it propagation into system. Experiments across diverse topologies and attack scenarios show that SAIGuard reduces attack success rates while maintaining MAS utility, outperforming reactive defenses.
booktitle: Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics: EMNLP 2026

title: Latent Personal Memory: Represent personal memory as dynamic soft prompts
abstract: Personalizing large language models (LLMs) requires encoding long-term, user-specific behavioral patterns in a way that is computationally efficient, scalable, and compatible with a frozen base model. We present Latent Personal Memory (LPM), a framework that represents user-specific history as a compact, persistent matrix of latent slots, that are interpretable. A shared cross-attention projection network maps these slots into dynamic, input-conditioned soft prompts that are prepended to the input of a frozen LLM. We evaluate LPM on PersonaMem v1 and LoCOMO benchmarks across Qwen3-1.7B, 4B, and 8B backbones. Results demonstrate that LPM outperforms LoRA and Prompt Tuning by up to 8.8 % and 54.4% in overall accuracy respectively on PersonaMem v1, while reducing KV-cache usage by over 64x. On LoCoMo, LPM matches LoRA’s accuracy while requiring approximately 120x fewer trainable parameters. We also show that LPM’s efficiency grows with context length and outperforms full-context at 128K context length.
booktitle: Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics: EMNLP 2026

title: Role Consistency in Role-Playing Agents: A Survey of Evaluation, Memory, Reasoning, Alignment, and Safety
abstract: Large language models have made role-playing agents viable as interactive characters, virtual companions, game agents, and social actors. The harder problem, however, is not producing one convincing response but sustaining a coherent role through long, changing, and sometimes adversarial interactions. This survey examines recent work on role consistency: the maintenance of identity, character knowledge, expressive style, memory, values, behavioral logic, and safety boundaries over time. We organize the literature around role specification, role-state maintenance, role-aware reasoning, role-consistent alignment, and evaluation.
booktitle: Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics: EMNLP 2026

title: Exploring LLMs for South Asian Music Understanding and Generation
abstract: Recent advancements in Large Language Models (LLMs) have shown promising results in music understanding and generation tasks. However, existing works remain confined to Western tonal traditions, offering little insight into whether current LLMs can handle structurally distinct low-resource musical traditions. We present the first systematic evaluation of LLM competence in South Asian classical music, a tradition governed by raga, tala-based melodic constraints that impose fundamentally different structural principles from Western harmony-driven music. We ground our evaluation in Hindustani classical theory and Bengali classical forms, including Rabindra and Nazrul Sangeet – representative low-resource traditions within South Asian classical music. For music understanding evaluation, we introduce a 504-question-answer benchmark spanning raga grammar, cultural knowledge, and symbolic notation reasoning, evaluating 33 LLMs where frontier models such as Gemini 2.5 Pro achieve 85-90% accuracy, while most open-source models remain in the 23-40% range. For music generation, we design a five-level controlled prompting framework and find that even the strongest model produces stylistically faithful outputs only 40% of the time. These results reveal that structural validity and stylistic faithfulness in music generation are distinct objectives and highlight an open challenge for culturally grounded music modeling.
booktitle: Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics: EMNLP 2026

title: Targeted Decoding Intervention for Persona Inconsistency Hallucination Mitigation in Multi-Turn Dialogue
abstract: Persona-driven role-playing agents tend to drift from their assigned profile or contradict their earlier statements as the dialogue lengthens, a faithfulness failure we call persona inconsistency hallucination. Existing inference-time mitigations apply reward-guided decoding uniformly at every token, while we observe that inconsistency risk is concentrated on a small subset of turns and is locally predictable, which makes a selective intervention feasible. We propose TaDI (Targeted Decoding Intervention), a training-free method with three components: an Inconsistency Risk Predictor that gates intervention before generation, a Targeted Reward-Guided Decoding module that combines a positive profile reward with a negative commitment reward, and a Commitment Propagation Memory that tracks the agent’s prior claims across turns. We additionally introduce a Type-A/B/C violation taxonomy distinguishing profile violation, history contradiction, and commitment fabrication, used as a diagnostic for attributing where any method gains or loses. Extensive experiments show TaDI is competitive with the strongest always-on baseline while being substantially more efficient and more robust under adversarial interrogation.
booktitle: Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics: EMNLP 2026

title: RxnExBench: Benchmarking Vision-Language Models for Structured Chemical Reaction Extraction from Scientific Literature
abstract: Screen Tables and Substrate Scopes are information-dense figures widely used in synthetic chemistry literature, yet automated extraction of structured reaction data from them remains challenging. We introduce RxnExBench, a multimodal benchmark for fine-grained reaction-level evaluation. Built from high-impact chemistry journals, it contains 3,565 expert-annotated reactions and 2,361 canonical molecular structures. The dataset adopts a unified schema with 15 reaction roles and 26 core fields, supporting downstream AI-for-Chemistry tasks such as retrosynthetic planning, yield prediction, and reaction condition recommendation. RxnExBench further provides a reasoning-driven difficulty taxonomy, a modular annotation pipeline, and the Oracle-MolRec protocol, which disentangles molecular recognition from higher-level reasoning. Evaluation of 9 state-of-the-art VLMs shows that performance degrades substantially as schema complexity and reasoning demands increase. Under the Oracle-MolRec setting, results further reveal that accurate molecular recognition alone is insufficient, with multimodal integration and chemistry-aware reasoning remaining the primary bottlenecks. We release all data and code to facilitate future research in chemistry-aware multimodal understanding and AI-for-Chemistry dataset construction.
booktitle: Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics: EMNLP 2026

title: FinGuard: Detecting Financial Regulatory Non-Compliance in LLM Interactions
abstract: As large language models (LLMs) are increasingly deployed in financial services, a single non-compliant interaction can expose institutions to regulatory penalties and direct consumer harm. Existing guard models are built around general harm taxonomies and overlook violations grounded in specific financial regulations. We address this gap with a regulation-driven pipeline that operates directly on regulatory documents, inducing a financial compliance risk taxonomy and synthesizing grounded training data without any predefined violation categories. Instantiating the pipeline on Chinese financial regulations, we release \textbf{FinGuard-Bench}, to our knowledge the first benchmark for financial regulatory compliance detection, with expert-annotated labels at both the query and response levels. We further train \textbf{FinGuard}, a financial compliance detection model built on Qwen3-8B and trained on the regulation-grounded data via supervised fine-tuning and self-play reinforcement learning. On FinGuard-Bench, FinGuard substantially outperforms all baselines, including dedicated guard models and much larger general-purpose LLMs such as Qwen3.5-397B-A17B and GPT-5.1. Furthermore, FinGuard also preserves general safety capabilities and adapts to unseen institution-specific policies using policy documents alone. We will publicly release the code, prompts, and resources used in this work on GitHub.
booktitle: Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics: EMNLP 2026

title: Temporal Tree of Thought: Reasoning-Guided Visual Cue Search for Long-Video Understanding
abstract: Long-video understanding remains challenging for Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) due to limited context length. Uniform sampling may miss crucial moments, while agent-based frame video understanding methods often evaluate frames independently, overlooking the temporal organization of videos. Ideally, evidence selection should mimic how humans answer questions about long videos: first locating the relevant segment from the global context, then zooming into local objects, and details. We propose Temporal Tree of Thought (T^3), a training-free framework for adaptive coarse-to-fine long-video understanding. T^3 constructs a question-agnostic hierarchical temporal tree via recursive temporally constrained clustering, where each node represents a contiguous segment with an informative key frame. During inference, T^3 performs an answer–retrieve–explore loop: it reasons over coarse representative frames, generates a search statement when evidence is insufficient, and expands relevant branches for finer-grained evidence. This process adaptively shifts the search target from temporal regions to specific objects, and visual details to help video understanding. Experiments on VideoMME, LongVideoBench, and LVBench show that T^3 improves Qwen2.5-VL-7B by 0.5%, 4.6%, and 4.4%, respectively, under the same frame budget, demonstrating the effectiveness of structured temporal reasoning. We will release code.
booktitle: Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics: EMNLP 2026

title: Sequential Beats Joint: On the Interplay between On-Policy Distillation and RLVR
abstract: Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) and on-policy distillation (OPD) have emerged as two dominant methods for post-training reasoning LLMs. Prior work uses OPD’s dense token-level supervision to complement the sparse RL reward, fusing the two signals within a single step: either as a weighted-additive combination or a teacher-modulated rescaling of the RL advantage. In this paper, we show that a simple two-stage scheme, OPD-then-RL, consistently outperforms pure OPD, pure RLVR, and all such joint baselines across logic and math reasoning benchmarks. Beyond the empirical results, we further provide a systematic understanding of this through pass@k behavior, learning dynamics, and parameter updates, yielding a consistent explanation: OPD expands the student’s coverage of teacher-supported solutions and RL sharpens within that support, while jointly optimizing the two signals causes them to interfere. To provide a practical recipe, we find that the OPD validation score is the key signal for when to switch to RL, and that OPD is a better cold start for RL than SFT. Together, our results establish OPD-then-RL as a simple yet strong way to combine the two methods, turning two entangled signals into complementary stages.
booktitle: Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics: EMNLP 2026

title: ETR: Outcome-Guided Elastic Trust Regions for Policy Optimization
abstract: Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards (RLVR) has emerged as an important paradigm for unlocking reasoning capabilities in large language models, exemplified by the success of OpenAI o1 and DeepSeek-R1. Currently, Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) stands as the dominant algorithm in this domain due to its stable training and critic-free efficiency. However, we argue that GRPO suffers from a structural limitation: it imposes a uniform, static trust region constraint across all samples. This design implicitly assumes signal homogeneity, a premise misaligned with the heterogeneous nature of outcome-driven learning, where advantage magnitudes and variances fluctuate significantly. Consequently, static constraints fail to fully exploit high-quality signals while insufficiently suppressing noise, often precipitating rapid entropy collapse. To address this, we propose **E**lastic **T**rust **R**egions (**ETR**), a dynamic mechanism that aligns optimization constraints with signal quality. ETR constructs a signal-aware landscape through dual-level elasticity: at the micro level, it scales clipping boundaries based on advantage magnitude to accelerate learning from high-confidence paths; at the macro level, it leverages group variance to implicitly allocate larger update budgets to tasks in the optimal learning zone. Extensive experiments on AIME and MATH benchmarks demonstrate that ETR consistently outperforms GRPO, achieving superior accuracy while effectively mitigating policy entropy degradation to ensure sustained exploration.
booktitle: Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics: EMNLP 2026

title: WhiFlash: Accelerating Speculative Decoding with Token-Level Cross-Paradigm Routing
abstract: The autoregressive nature of large language models (LLMs) remains a significant bottleneck for inference, particularly in complex agentic workloads. While speculative decoding (SD) accelerates inference, current approaches rely on static drafting paradigms, utilising either autoregressive drafting models for reasoning or diffusion-based parallel models for structured outputs. We empirically find that drafting accuracy fluctuates dramatically within a single sequence, leaving significant performance unrealised by static paradigms and coarse-grained routing. To address this volatility, we introduce WhiFlash, the first cross-paradigm SD method that unifies autoregressive and diffusion-based parallel drafting under a single token-level controller. WhiFlash adopts a fine-grained routing mechanism that employs either a lightweight entropy-based or a learned neural policy, both parametrised to provide a tunable balance between expected token gain and latency. To make high-frequency switching computationally viable, we introduce novel cache-management optimisations, Lazy Catch-up and KV-only Prefill, reducing switching overhead to below 6% of per-round latency. By capitalising on the complementary strengths of fundamentally distinct drafting architectures, WhiFlash achieves significantly higher acceptance lengths, yielding category-specific throughput gains of up to 69.6% over the state-of-the-art autoregressive EAGLE-3 and 37.3% over the diffusion-based DFlash.
booktitle: Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics: EMNLP 2026

title: BlueprintAgent: Constraint-Triggered Targeted Revisits for Simulation-Ready Generation from Scanned Structural Blueprints
abstract: Converting in-service reinforced-concrete (RC) building blueprints into simulation-ready models underpins safety assessment and seismic retrofit, but the process remains largely manual. Direct prompting of a multimodal large language model (MLLM) over a full scanned sheet is unreliable: plausible-looking outputs often violate engineering constraints on beam–column support, span count, or 3D continuity.We present BlueprintAgent (BPA), a constraint-triggered multimodal agent for simulation-ready frame extraction from scanned blueprints. BPA treats the MLLM as the primary reader and decision maker, with OCR and computer vision supplying localized evidence. Its novelty is not the tool stack but a control mechanism: engineering constraints are realized as callable validators whose entity-level conflict reports trigger targeted MLLM revisits over the relevant local region—an inference-time control distinct from fixed pipelines and free-form self-reflection.We evaluate BPA on 300 real scanned blueprint sheets from 20 anonymized RC frame projects, against five baselines and six ablations. BPA reaches a macro-averaged Beam F1 of 0.994, against 0.301 for single-MLLM zero-shot and 0.820 for a fixed pipeline; removing MLLM-led axis adjudication collapses Beam and Column F1 on complex multi-sheet projects. For dense technical drawings, engineering constraints are best deployed as triggers for entity-level targeted revisits rather than as post-hoc output filters.
booktitle: Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics: EMNLP 2026

title: Beyond the Sampled Token: Preserving Candidate Support in RLVR
abstract: We revisit exploration collapse in reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR), from the perspective of the candidate distribution for next-token prediction. We formally show that as probability concentrates on the top-1 candidate, the expected number of distinct responses collapses to one regardless of the sampling budget K. This theoretical implication is further verified by our empirical tracking of top-N candidate probabilities during training, where the top-1 candidate progressively dominates while plausible alternatives are suppressed. These findings suggest a key desideratum for effective exploration: preserving non-negligible probability mass on the top-N candidates. To this end, we propose Candidate-aware Support Preservation (CaSP), with two complementary designs. Specifically, CaSP redistributes positive gradients among top-N candidates for correct responses, and applies a stronger penalty to the top-1 candidate for incorrect responses. Unlike many exploration-oriented methods that improve pass@K at the cost of pass@1, CaSP improves pass@K across the full K spectrum. These gains generalize to 6 math, 2 logical-reasoning, and 2 coding benchmarks, and scales to 32B-parameter models and sampling budgets up to K=1024, positioning it as a principled, candidate-level approach for RLVR exploration.
booktitle: Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics: EMNLP 2026

title: ARC: An Audit-Guided Risk Calibration Attack for Jailbreaking Multimodal Large Language Models
