title: LongPIBench: A Long-Context Benchmark for Prompt Injection
abstract: Prompt injection attacks pose a serious security risk to large language models in real-world applications. However, existing prompt injection benchmarks primarily focus on short-context inputs, leaving the attacks and defenses in long-context settings largely unexplored. This gap leads to a substantial overestimation of the effectiveness of current defenses. In this paper, we bridge the gap by introducing LongPIBench, a long-context benchmark for prompt injection covering 4 realistic application scenarios: paper peer review, resume screening, code review, and email summary. For each scenario, we construct a synthetic dataset and a real-world dataset, with context lengths ranging from thousands to tens of thousands of tokens. The evaluation results on LongPIBench reveal significant vulnerabilities of prompt injection defenses under long-context settings: even simple heuristic prompt injection attacks achieve high success rates and frequently bypass state-of-the-art defenses. We hope LongPIBench can serve as a practical benchmark for systematically evaluating prompt injection defenses in realistic long-context scenarios.
booktitle: Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics: EMNLP 2026

title: Agent4Weakness: An Agentic Framework for In-Depth Model Weakness Discovery
abstract: The rapid evolution of reasoning-intensive Large Language Models renders traditional metrics insufficient by masking fine-grained failures and implicit pathologies. Existing weakness discovery methods typically rely on rigid pipelines, yielding superficial insights that lack the diagnostic depth required for effective model improvement. To address this, we introduce Agent4Weakness, a multi-agent framework designed to replicate the rigorous workflow of human expert analysts. By integrating a Domain-Aware Memory for contextual reasoning with diagnostic evaluation skills and a Tool Abstraction mechanism for decouple data analysis, Agent4Weakness transforms raw evaluation traces into grounded, actionable reports. We validate our framework through an extensive study involving 104 models across 27 benchmarks. Experimental results demonstrate that Agent4Weakness produces diagnostic reports significantly superior to competitive baselines. Crucially, leveraging these insights for prompt guidance yields an average 3.7 point performance boost and establishes a closed-loop optimization framework.
booktitle: Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics: EMNLP 2026

title: MedCalc-Pro: Solving Complex Medical Calculations with LLM Agents
abstract: Current benchmarks for evaluating large language models (LLMs) in medical calculation are largely based on simplified settings, where each patient case corresponds to a single calculator and the required tool is explicitly specified in the query. However, real clinical scenarios often require multiple calculators for joint evaluation, nested-calculator calculation, and fuzzy queries that do not directly specify the target calculator. To this end, we propose a new medical calculation benchmark, MedCalc-Pro, which covers three progressively challenging task settings: single-calculator, multi-calculator, and nested-calculator calculation settings. MedCalc-Pro contains 2,268 real-world clinical cases, covering 77 medical calculators across 14 clinical departments. Meanwhile, to address the limited performance of existing frameworks and methods in complex clinical scenarios, we further propose a more generalizable agent framework that supports multi-calculator selection and nested-calculator calling, while suppressing parameter error propagation through structured validation and evidence audit. We conduct systematic comparisons across open-source, closed-source, and medical-specialized LLMs, and the results show that our framework achieves the best performance across all three task settings. This work provides a new benchmark and method for evaluating and applying LLMs in challenging medical calculation scenarios. The dataset and code are publicly available at https://github.com/easymoney7774/MedCalc-Pro.
booktitle: Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics: EMNLP 2026

title: Retrieval-Augmented Simplification of Sectioned Biomedical Abstracts
abstract: Cochrane systematic reviews pair each technical abstract with a plain-language summary (PLS), but most biomedical papers lack a PLS. We propose a retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) pipeline that generates Cochrane PLS from biomedical abstracts. The pipeline exploits the section-level alignment of the Cochrane-sections dataset in two ways. First, it provides the LLM with abstract-PLS section pairs from topically related reviews, giving more granular in-context examples than whole abstract-PLS pairs. Second, each retrieved PLS section is split into its rephrased and inserted sentences, showing the LLM both the rephrasing and the insertion behavior it should reproduce. Our pipeline outperforms a non-RAG LLM and three RAG ablations on the Cochrane-sections test set, with the same gain trend across three different LLM families.
booktitle: Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics: EMNLP 2026

title: FaVOR: LLM-Based Agentic Framework for Factor Mining via Empirical Validation
abstract: Traditional finance relies on experts to hand-craft factors through a principled process grounded in economic rationale. Recent LLM-based multi-agent systems have automated this process, scaling factor mining far beyond manual effort. However, these automated approaches optimize directly for returns and rarely check whether a generated factor still expresses the economic hypothesis that motivated it. We identify this inconsistency between mathematical form and economic meaning as a structural failure mode of return-oriented automation. The resulting factors blur the line between real signals and spurious correlations and break down across regime shifts. We propose FaVOR (Factor Validation through Observable Reasoning), an agentic framework that restructures factor mining around hypothesis-level evidence rather than return outcomes. In place of the standard hypothesis-to-formula leap, FaVOR enforces a three-stage consistency loop tying mathematical form to economic rationale throughout. (1) Decomposition splits a broad economic hypothesis into independent observable conditions. (2) Validation checks whether each factor reflects its intended condition. (3) Integration merges them into a composite whose structure remains interpretable. On the CSI 500 and S P 500 in 2025, FaVOR outperforms existing baselines while remaining effective across regimes. FaVOR shows that hypothesis-grounded factor discovery produces signals that are interpretable by construction, regime-robust, and economically faithful. The code is available at https://github.com/damilab/FaVOR.
booktitle: Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics: EMNLP 2026

title: Decision Rigidity in LLM Disinformation Detection: Behavioral and Representational Evidence
abstract: LLMs deployed as judges in high-stakes classification are commonly assumed to let their generated rationale shape the verdict; we show this assumption fails in disinformation detection. We introduce the Multi-Bias Injection Protocol (MBIP), which perturbs the reasoning stage along four cognitive axes (confirmation, anchoring, framing, authority) while holding the input fixed, and quantifies induced rationale variation with technique-count metrics anchored on the number of persuasion techniques the model reports. Across five disinformation datasets, MBIP produces substantial rationale variation but near-zero verdict flipping; an explicit rationale-deference prompt raises the flip rate only modestly, to 0.118–0.300 across three open-weight models, with API-only gpt-4o-mini in the same range. We call this verdict-level invariance Decision Rigidity. At the representational level, our residual-stream probe localizes a candidate commitment band late in the network, where biased and neutral final-class trajectories converge. The band’s location is architectural, replicated by a neutral-vs-neutral null; a within-band alignment-rate elevation and a random-lexicon control gap co-occur with the behavioral invariance and attenuate in Gemma-2-9B. All representational evidence is correlational. Generalization to other high-prior, evidence-dependent classifications and attenuation on reasoning-intensive tasks remain falsifiable hypotheses.
booktitle: Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics: EMNLP 2026

title: Decouple and Orthogonalize: A Data-Free Framework for LoRA Merging
abstract: With the growing availability of open-source task-specific models, model merging has become a practical way to combine multiple models into one. However, existing studies mainly focus on fully fine-tuned models and overlook widely used LoRA modules. We show that full fine-tuning merging methods perform poorly on LoRA due to its larger cross-task magnitude disparities, which distort merged parameters and degrade performance. To address this, we propose DO-Merging (Decouple and Orthogonalize), a data-free framework for LoRA merging. Specifically, we decompose model weights into magnitude and direction components and merge them independently, preventing magnitude imbalances from distorting the merged direction. We further introduce a layer-wise gradient descent method with orthogonal constraints that reduces inter-task interference among direction components without requiring any training data. We provide theoretical analysis supporting both components. Extensive experiments across vision, language, and multi-modal domains show that DO-Merging consistently outperforms existing methods, achieving up to 5% gains on vision tasks, with negligible additional cost. Both parts can be integrated into existing merging methods as plug-and-play enhancements.
booktitle: Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics: EMNLP 2026

title: ReasonMap: Making Implicit Mathematical Knowledge Explicit in Long Chain-of-Thought Traces
abstract: Long chain-of-thought (CoT) traces provide observable natural-language rationales for mathematical problem solving, but they rarely expose the named definitions and theorems that justify the written solution. We treat each problem–trace pair as carrying a recoverable knowledge footprint: a trace-grounded support set of named definitions and theorems. Inspired by formal proofs, where supporting premises are recorded more explicitly than in free-form CoT, we formulate Mathematical Support Set Extraction (MSSE): given a problem and a completed long CoT trace, recover the canonical support set that supports the written solution. We propose ReasonMap, which attributes this support set to make solutions auditable, reusable, and easier to repair. ReasonMap follows a two-stage pipeline: proof-to-CoT support transfer adapts premise-explicit proof supervision to premise-implicit long CoT traces, and hard-negative support calibration applies preference optimization against plausible-but-wrong support sets. Experiments show that ReasonMap improves support-set extraction over strong baselines and that ReasonMap-generated support hints aid downstream reasoning in both frontier-model and self-generated settings. The GitHub repository is available at https://github.com/kui253/ReasonMap.
booktitle: Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics: EMNLP 2026

title: VizRAG: Enhancing Retrieval-Augmented Generation with Hypergraph Visualization
abstract: Hypergraph-based RAG systems surpass traditional graph-based approaches by organizing complex n-ary atomic facts among entities, rather than relying solely on binary relationships. Despite the advancements in multimodal large language models (MLLMs) with enhanced visual capabilities, current hypergraph-based RAG frameworks predominantly restrict knowledge retrieval and reconstruction to a unimodal, text-centric paradigm. This limitation prevents them from fully leveraging the powerful visual perception capabilities of modern MLLMs. To address this gap, we systematically explore the integration of hypergraph awareness in RAG systems through visual cues. By incorporating visual representations of hypergraphs into the RAG pipeline, we introduce VizRAG, the first RAG system to support visual hypergraph structure awareness. Experimental results demonstrate that VizRAG significantly outperforms strong baselines, validating the promising potential of hypergraph visualization as a novel approach for RAG systems.
booktitle: Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics: EMNLP 2026

title: HuggingBrew: Brewing High-Quality Mid-Training Data from the HuggingFace Community Datasets
abstract: Data curation for large language models (LLMs) has been extensively studied for both the pre-training and post-training stages, yet the intermediate \textit{mid-training} phase—bridging general pretraining and  task-specific fine-tuning—remains critically underexplored. Most existing mid-training data for state-of-the-art models remains proprietary. Meanwhile, the Hugging Face platform hosts a huge amount of community-contributed datasets, yet no systematic effort has been made to refine this rich ecosystem into a unified high-quality corpus. We present \textbf{HuggingBrew}, a large-scale mid-training corpus constructed through a principled, multi-step curation pipeline applied to the massive publicly accessible Hugging Face datasets. The pipeline operates at two complementary granularities: \textit{dataset-level} operations act on each dataset independently, while \textit{corpus-level} operations are applied jointly across all retained corpus. We construct three progressively curated variants—\textsf{Draught}, \textsf{Craft}, and \textsf{Reserve}—containing 1.6T, 450B, and 40B tokens, respectively. Continual pretraining experiments under a 100B-token budget show that series yields substantial improvements over baselines across mathematical reasoning, general knowledge, and code generation, validating the untapped value of community-contributed data for mid-training.
booktitle: Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics: EMNLP 2026

title: Transition Overlap: Construction-Time Conditioning for Position-Independent KV Cache Reuse
abstract: In long context applications like Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG), Large Language Models (LLMs) often reuse independently precomputed Key Value (KV) caches to reduce latency. However, directly assembling these cached segments introduces errors that degrade generation quality. We study this problem in the setting of position-independent caching and decompose the reuse error into two components: a geometric error (G) caused by position mismatch, which can be largely removed by position alignment, and a dynamic error (D) caused by context-dependent representation changes. To characterize D, we introduce the smoothness gap, a local diagnostic that measures the discrepancy between local KV-state transitions in isolated caches and those in the full-context baseline. This gap serves as a necessary local consistency diagnostic for reconstruction errors across adjacent positions and reveals that recomputing non-contiguous selected tokens can introduce additional transition discontinuities, thereby amplifying the dynamic error. To overcome this limitation, we propose Transition Overlap, a training-free cache-construction protocol that prepends a short temporary overlap to approximate full-context boundary transitions and stores only the KV states of the original segment tokens. We instantiate it under two deployment regimes: Self-Segment Overlap (SSO) for query-independent offline caches and Cross-Segment Overlap (CSO) for cases in which the predecessor segment is known during construction. In both evaluated deployment settings, Transition Overlap improves the measured serving latency–quality trade-off over training-free PIC baselines[Code is available at <https://github.com/boyoi/Transition-Overlap>].
booktitle: Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics: EMNLP 2026

title: PrAM: Offline Checkpoint Selection for Post-Hoc Training Data Attribution
abstract: Training data attribution scores how training examples affect downstream model performance. For models released with many intermediate checkpoints, attribution can be computed along the saved training trajectory, but evaluating every checkpoint is often prohibitively expensive. We introduce PrAM (Probe-based Attribution Mass), a post-hoc offline checkpoint selector for training data attribution. PrAM runs a small attribution probe at every checkpoint, selects checkpoints with high absolute attribution mass, and runs full attribution only on that subset. Across Pythia-14M, 70M, and 160M, PrAM closely matches a full attribution-pool reference and outperforms heuristic rules based on recency, spacing, learning rate, and validation loss. Beyond rank correlation, PrAM preserves the domain-by-target attribution tables and ranked training examples produced by full saved-checkpoint attribution, enabling scalable post-hoc analyses of checkpointed model releases. We support this with application-based analyses scaling to 410M and 1B parameter models.
booktitle: Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics: EMNLP 2026

title: Counterfactual Self-Distillation: A Distribution-Shaping Framework for Entity-Fact Unlearning in Large Language Models
abstract: Entity-fact unlearning in large language models (LLMs) aims to remove the binding between a target entity and a forgotten fact, producing a model that behaves like one retrained without the forgotten data while preserving neighboring knowledge and overall model utility. We frame this problem as distribution shaping: such a retrained model would yield a plausible distribution at forget queries, fluent, semantically appropriate, and reflective of residual knowledge, which we take as the appropriate target. Existing objectives provide only narrow token-level or semantically uninformative supervision, falling short of this target. We propose Counterfactual Self-Distillation (CSD), a self-distillation framework that approximates the retrained distribution by constructing a counterfactual teacher through type-consistent entity substitution. The resulting teacher is decoupled from the target identity while preserving type-level relational structure, enabling directed probability reallocation without an external oracle. Experiments on TOFU and RWKU show that CSD achieves a strong forget-utility trade-off, including the best overall forgetting on RWKU and strong performance on TOFU.
booktitle: Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics: EMNLP 2026

title: Why Knowing Both Hops Is Not Enough: Understanding Two-Hop Generalization in Language Models
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) can solve complex multi-hop problems yet exhibit puzzling failures on simple two-hop queries: although a model may correctly store each individual hop, it often fails to combine them. To understand the internal mechanisms of this phenomenon, we train transformers from scratch in a controlled symbolic environment. Our experiments reveal a pattern in two-hop generalization: models generalize reliably when the second hop follows the training distribution, but always fail when it deviates. Through mechanistic analysis, we provide a complete explanation for these distinct generalization behaviors: in settings where models generalize successfully, performance is driven by the emergence of consistent intermediate representations for the same entities across contexts, whereas failures on settings where the second hop is out-of-distribution arise from a mismatch across layers: lower layers correctly construct these intermediate representations, but upper layers, while trained on corresponding atomic facts, primarily learn to map them to outputs rather than to reason over them. Driven by this insight, we propose a recurrent-style training strategy, which enables transformers to reuse their reasoning circuitry across input forms and substantially improves generalization on out-of-distribution two-hop queries. Our data and code are available at https://github.com/zzl-strong/two_hop.
booktitle: Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics: EMNLP 2026

title: Unified Fragment Growing, Linking, and Merging with Energy-Aware Pre-training and Reward-Ranked Alignment
abstract: Fragment-based drug discovery optimizes small molecular hits through three recurring transformations: fragment growing, linking, and merging. Existing generative methods, however, usually specialize in a single transformation and have focused primarily on linker design. We introduce FragmentGPT, a unified chemical language model that casts all three operations as conditional molecular generation. To build this capability, we construct a chemically-aware pre-training corpus using energy-guided bond cleavage, together with overlap-based examples that teach the model to connect separated fragments and consolidate shared substructures. We further introduce Reward-Ranked Alignment with Expert Exploration (RAE), which combines expert-guided candidate generation, Pareto- and composite-reward-based selection, and supervised fine-tuning for multi-objective molecular optimization. Conditioned on one or more fragments, FragmentGPT can expand a scaffold, connect distinct subunits, or merge overlapping structures into a complete molecule. Experiments on RTCB and SARS-CoV-2 main protease (3CLPro), together with ablation studies, show high chemical validity and strong aggregate performance across multiple drug-design objectives.
booktitle: Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics: EMNLP 2026

title: HoloDP: A Multilingual Benchmark Suite and Script-Aware Framework for Document Parsing
abstract: Millions of multilingual documents remain locked in image formats, but current document parsers are still largely evaluated and optimized for a narrow range of high-resource languages and regular writing layouts. As a result, their reliability drops sharply when facing underrepresented scripts, vertical or right-to-left writing, and mixed-script document structures. We present HoloDP, a multilingual benchmark suite and script-aware framework for document parsing. HoloDP first introduces a standardized evaluation suite covering 13 languages across seven script families, with tasks spanning page-level layout analysis, region-level parsing, and mixed-script structural composition. Built on this resource, HoloDP further develops a script-aware parser that combines a Swin Transformer encoder, a four-branch direction-adaptive vision-to-text module, and a multilingual decoder. The adaptive module explicitly captures horizontal, vertical, diagonal, and global spatial priors, enabling the model to better handle heterogeneous writing systems and layouts. Extensive experiments show that HoloDP delivers consistent gains on underrepresented and mixed-script benchmarks while remaining competitive on high-resource Chinese and English documents. Ablation studies confirm that the benchmark resources, direction-aware adaptation, and script-conditioned modeling provide complementary benefits. We will release the code, models, and benchmarks for further research.
booktitle: Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics: EMNLP 2026

title: LookBack: Where and How to Score LVLM Responses via Visual Reference Usage
abstract: Large Vision-Language Models (LVLMs) integrate visual perception with language generation, enabling responses that span image understanding and complex reasoning. However, LVLMs do not just inherit the text-level hallucinations; they also hallucinate against the image, producing fluent responses ungrounded in what they see. This makes LVLM response scoring inherently harder, and our diagnostics show that existing confidence-based metrics adopted from LLMs is insufficient for LVLMs. Specifically, removing the input image barely changes confidence-based selection, suggesting that output-space confidence primarily captures textual plausibility rather than agreement with the image. To address this gap, we propose LookBack, a training-free LVLM response scoring method that augments token likelihood with visual lookback score, a lightweight measure of how strongly each response token refers to image tokens. Across four benchmarks and three models, LookBack consistently improves Best-of- selection over existing baselines with negligible additional overhead.
booktitle: Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics: EMNLP 2026

title: LogitsCoder: Towards Efficient Chain-of-Thought Path Search via Logits Preference Decoding for Code Generation
abstract: Code generation requires executable reasoning, making test-time chain-of-thought (CoT) search an attractive strategy for improving solution quality. However, existing CoT scaling methods often face a tension between underthinking, where shallow reasoning misses important algorithmic cases, and overthinking, where verbose or redundant reasoning consumes substantial tokens without improving correctness. We propose LogitsCoder, a lightweight framework that revisits CoT search from the perspective of logits-level control. LogitsCoder improves efficient reasoning search through two complementary mechanisms: Logits Preference Decoding adaptively calibrates local token expansion using public-test feedback, while Logits Rank Based Path Selection explores and selects compact high-confidence reasoning trajectories based on logit-level stability. Together with Thoughts Aggregation, LogitsCoder refines reasoning paths without relying on costly MCTS-style tree expansion. Extensive experiments demonstrate that LogitsCoder produces more efficient and higher-quality reasoning chains, leading to superior code generation performance compared to baseline methods.
booktitle: Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics: EMNLP 2026

title: Towards Generalizable Visually Grounded Exploration of Household Devices
abstract: Recent advancements in Vision-Language Models (VLMs) have demonstrated impressive capabilities in static visual recognition and high-level semantic reasoning. However, current embodied exploration paradigms still heavily rely on imitation learning from human-annotated trajectories, which severely limits agents’ generalization ability. The key bottleneck of realizing general autonomous embodied agents lies in Generalizable Visually Grounded Exploration—the ability to operate novel devices without manuals or specific training by actively grounding abstract world knowledge into fine-grained visual affordances. Yet, existing benchmarks fail to evaluate this capability: they generally rely on explicit documents and annotated trajectories, neglecting the dynamic Hypothesis-Interaction-Refinement process essential for functional device operation. To bridge this gap, we introduce VGEBench, a comprehensive benchmark designed to evaluate the generalizable visually grounded exploration capabilities of VLMs. Unlike static datasets, we construct a Logic-Driven State Machine framework. This framework simulates multi-turn interaction loops, compelling agents to achieve goals by active visual perception and feedback-driven correction. Experimental results demonstrate that existing VLMs face significant challenges in translating semantic knowledge into physical execution and maintaining long-horizon state tracking.
booktitle: Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics: EMNLP 2026

title: HybridProver: Augmenting Theorem Proving with LLM-Driven Proof Synthesis and Refinement
abstract: Formal methods play a crucial role in ensuring the reliability of critical systems through rigorous mathematical verification. However, their adoption remains limited due to the labor-intensive nature of manual proof construction. Recent advances in large language models (LLMs) have opened new opportunities for automated theorem proving. Two main paradigms have emerged: stepwise tactic-based generation and whole-proof synthesis. While both approaches have complementary strengths, existing work largely treats them in isolation. In this work, we propose HybridProver, a unified framework that integrates whole-proof synthesis and tactic-based generation through proof sketches as an intermediate representation. This design enables the reuse of partially correct proof structures while effectively combining high-level planning with fine-grained reasoning. We implement HybridProver in Isabelle/HOL and post-train two 7B-scale LLMs on our optimized Isabelle datasets. Experiments on the miniF2F Isabelle benchmark achieved a 73.8% success rate and improved upon the previous state of the art (61.9%), demonstrating that lightweight models, when combined with our approach, can effectively generate Isabelle/HOL proofs without relying on very large LLMs. Ablation studies further analyze the impact of dataset quality, training configurations, and sampling strategies on proof generation. All code and datasets are released.
booktitle: Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics: EMNLP 2026

title: HyperPathsRAG: Multi-Target Path Approximation over Hypergraph Knowledge Graphs for Multi-Hop QA
abstract: Multi-hop question answering needs evidence that is scattered across many sentences and ordered along a reasoning chain. Existing RAG systems struggle with this setting because flat chunk retrieval can miss bridge facts, binary graph structures lose n-ary information, and unordered top-K contexts leave evidence composition to the answer model. We introduce HyperPathsRAG, a hypergraph-based RAG framework that aligns query decomposition with the corpus index. It decomposes questions into n-ary sub-questions aligned with hypergraph facts, jointly matches all sub-questions to retrieve reasoning paths, scores paths by chain completeness, and presents the retrieved evidence in reasoning order. We evaluate in the candidate-passage setting on the 1k-question hard subsets of HotpotQA, 2Wiki, and MuSiQue, with three answering LLMs. HyperPathsRAG attains the best average Exact Match on every backbone (up to 42.2 EM / 56.2 F1 with Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct), and the best average F1 on two of three backbones; ablations attribute the bulk of the gain to the hypergraph index and the multi-target retriever. Our code is available at https://anonymous.4open.science/r/HyperPathsRAG-AE05/.
booktitle: Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics: EMNLP 2026

title: GRAIN: Bridging Name and Narrative Shifts in Real-World Graph Reasoning through Invariance-Rewarded Agentic RL
abstract: Despite their potential in standardized graph tasks, Large Language Models (LLMs) remain brittle to real-world shifts in node identifiers and task formulation. While deterministic graph tools are invariant to such shifts, extracting topological structures from noisy text is highly fragile for LLMs, which often overfit to surface patterns. Moreover, mitigating these parsing failures via multi-agent systems incurs prohibitive latency. To address this, we propose GRAIN, a single-agent framework optimized via reinforcement learning. GRAIN models reasoning as a semantic parsing and tool-execution pipeline, guided by a Structure Invariance Reward. By validating extracted intermediate graphs against ground-truth topologies, this reward forces the LLM to learn robust text-to-structure mappings rather than memorizing linguistic artifacts. We also introduce GRIT, a benchmark evaluating sensitivity to such linguistic shifts. GRAIN outperforms multi-agent baselines by 16.45% in accuracy with approximately 24% lower latency. Furthermore, it demonstrates superior structural generalization, halving the out-of-distribution (OOD) gap of SFT models (from 15.77% to 7.80%) and maintaining robustness on large-scale graphs beyond the training distribution.
booktitle: Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics: EMNLP 2026

title: Counterfactual Selective Imitation for Long-Horizon Agents
abstract: Long-horizon agents with structured actions execute tasks through sequences of dependent decisions, so a local decision mistake can change later observations and cause the task to fail. Stronger expert models offer a natural source of supervision, yet direct imitation or behavior cloning treats many differences between expert and base actions as equally useful targets. In this paper, we propose counterfactual selective imitation (CSI), a method that uses same-state counterfactual comparison to identify positive return differences. CSI assigns expert targets only when counterfactual rollouts show a high positive return difference, and routine states receive base-policy targets. The learned update is restricted to structured action spans, leaves the base model frozen, and does not require expert queries or replay at deployment. Experiments on AppWorld, ToolSandbox, and WebShop show that CSI raises average task success from 33.3% to 49.7% over the Qwen3-8B base and reduces average invalid/tool error from 9.3% to 4.9%. Compared with the strongest same-deployment adaptation baseline, CSI improves average task success by 1.3 points with only 5% additional deployed-inference latency.
booktitle: Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics: EMNLP 2026

title: Ada-SQL: Efficient and Adaptive Reasoning for Text-to-SQL
abstract: Reasoning efficiency in Text-to-SQL is an important yet underexplored problem. Chain-of-Thought (CoT) reasoning models simplify traditional Text-to-SQL workflows and significantly improve the ability to handle complex queries. However, existing methods typically generate long reasoning processes for all queries. This leads to high token consumption and inference latency, increasing system cost and limiting practical deployment. To address this issue, we propose Ada-SQL, an adaptive reasoning model for Text-to-SQL that jointly optimizes reasoning mode selection and token budget control via a two-stage reinforcement learning framework coupled with a token budget model. This enables the model to adaptively decide whether to reason and how much reasoning budget to allocate based on query difficulty. Experimental results show that Ada-SQL reduces output token consumption by more than 65% while maintaining competitive execution accuracy, achieving a favorable performance-efficiency trade-off. Code and models will be released at https://github.com/sxhText2SQL/Ada-SQL.
booktitle: Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics: EMNLP 2026

title: Beyond Gradient Egalitarianism: Dual-Adaptive C-AUM Framework for Few-Shot Fine-Tuning of Large Language Models
abstract: While large language models (LLMs) demonstrate strong text classification capabilities, adapting them to specialized, few-shot industrial domains remains challenging. Vanilla supervised fine-tuning (SFT) applies uniform weighting to training samples and may overfit easy instances while insufficiently optimizing ambiguous boundary samples. Static regularization may further limit adaptation by applying the same constraint throughout training. To address these limitations, we propose cumulative area under the margin (C-AUM), a fine-tuning framework tailored to autoregressive LLM classification. C-AUM tracks the cumulative margin of the final decision token as an instance-level difficulty signal and uses it to coordinate AUM-aware instance weighting with difficulty-aware dynamic LoRA regularization. We also construct and release an expert-verified few-shot text classification benchmark for the steel industry, comprising 1,070 samples across seven fine-grained categories. Evaluations across six representative LLMs show that C-AUM achieves comparable or improved performance over vanilla SFT, with a maximum macro F1 gain of 1.99 percentage points. Our dataset and code are publicly available at https://github.com/pengdada98/C-AUM.
booktitle: Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics: EMNLP 2026

title: Interpretable Oracle Bone Script Decipherment via Progressive Glyph Analysis with LVLMs
abstract: Deciphering scanned Oracle Bone Script (OBS) images into corresponding modern Chinese characters is a crucial step in AI-assisted OBS decipherment. As a highly pictographic writing system, OBS often embeds semantic information in glyph forms, making its decipherment depend on more than visual similarity alone. However, how to effectively exploit such glyph-meaning cues and how to make the decipherment process interpretable remain challenging. To this end, we propose an LVLM-based framework that bridges glyphs and meanings through structured glyph analysis. Specifically, we introduce a progressive training strategy that guides the model from radical analysis to pictographic analysis and finally to mutual analysis, enabling it to capture semantic information embedded in OBS glyphs. The generated textual analyses serve as both interpretable reasoning traces and explicit evidence for retrieving corresponding modern Chinese characters from a dictionary. We also construct the Pictographic Decipherment OBS Dataset (PD-OBS), which provides detailed radical and pictographic analyses to support glyph-analysis learning and dictionary-based retrieval. Experiments on OBS benchmarks demonstrate the strong zero-shot capability of our method, especially its substantially improved Top-10 accuracy on unseen OBS, highlighting its ability to provide reliable and interpretable candidate references for AI-assisted archaeological and historical studies. The code and dataset will be released at https://github.com/PKXX1943/PD-OBS.
booktitle: Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics: EMNLP 2026

title: NUM2EVENT: Structured Event Inference from Numerical Time-Series
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) have shown strong multimodal reasoning abilities, yet their understanding of purely numerical time-series remains limited. Existing approaches mainly focus on forecasting or trend description, providing little insight into the underlying events that have occurred or are unfolding within observed numerical dynamics. We study number-to-event reasoning and decoding, a task that infers interpretable and structured event hypotheses directly from numerical time-series when explicit event information is unavailable at inference time. The task focuses on aligned and plausible event semantics that help explain observed numerical dynamics. To address data scarcity and semantic alignment challenges, we propose a reasoning-aware framework that combines an agent-guided event extractor, a Hawkes-process-based synthetic data generator, and a multi-stage fine-tuning pipeline integrating a time-series encoder with a structured event decoder. The model generates intermediate reasoning steps and outputs constrained event representations. Experiments across multiple real-world domains show that our approach consistently outperforms strong LLM baselines in event-level precision and recall, demonstrating its effectiveness in bridging numerical reasoning and semantic event understanding. The code is available at https://github.com/feng1201/NUM2EVENT_IDEA
booktitle: Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics: EMNLP 2026

title: CQA-Eval: Designing Reliable Evaluations of Multi-paragraph Clinical QA under Resource Constraints
abstract: Evaluating multi-paragraph clinical question answering (QA) systems is resource-intensive and challenging: accurate judgments require medical expertise and achieving consistent human judgments over multi-paragraph text is difficult. We introduce CQA-Eval, an evaluation framework and set of evaluation recommendations for limited-resource and high-expertise settings. Based on physician annotations of 300 real patient questions answered by physicians and LLMs, we compare coarse answer-level versus fine-grained sentence-level evaluation over the dimensions of correctness, relevance, and risk disclosure. We find that inter-annotator agreement (IAA) varies by dimension: fine-grained annotation improves agreement on correctness, coarse improves agreement on relevance, and judgments on communicates-risks remain inconsistent. Additionally, annotating only a small subset of sentences can provide reliability comparable to coarse annotations, reducing cost and effort. Data and code available at https://github.com/federicabologna/cqa-eval under a CC-BY license.
booktitle: Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics: EMNLP 2026

title: APEX-Searcher: Hierarchical Credit Assignment with Subgoaling for Agentic Retrieval-Augmented Generation
abstract: Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) connects large language models (LLMs) to external knowledge, but single-round retrieval is often insufficient for complex multi-hop questions. To improve search on complex tasks, most existing works combine multi-round retrieval with reasoning through end-to-end training. While these approaches improve problem-solving performance, they still face challenges in task reasoning and model training. First, due to the lack of an explicit subgoaling mechanism, most existing RAG methods may produce ambiguous retrieval execution paths, leading to the degradation of model performance. Second, a few existing RAG methods have started to incorporate planning and execution into the model training process. However, they typically rely on a single final reward, causing hierarchical credit entanglement between planning and execution and preventing the model from clearly separating plan errors from retrieval errors. To address these limitations, we propose APEX-Searcher, a coordinated planner–executor framework that optimizes a recursive planner with RL to accommodate multiple valid, dependency-aware decompositions while training the executor with SFT under clearer subtask-level supervision. Extensive experiments show consistent gains in both multi-hop RAG and task planning across benchmarks.
booktitle: Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics: EMNLP 2026

title: When AI-Text Detectors Become Evidence: Rethinking Detection for Human Decisions
abstract: AI-generated-text detectors are evaluated as classifiers, yet consequential deployments use detector outputs as evidence that people inspect, trust, contest, or use to escalate decisions. We call this mismatch the classification–evidence gap. The gap makes scalar detector scores a weak deployment interface: they hide the basis of a judgment, invite overtrust, and can turn false positives into accusations. We argue that AI-text detection should be evaluated as evidence-grounded decision support rather than as authorship proof. We introduce AGENT-XTrust, a guideline-expert detector that returns direct MetaAgent labels without target-domain scalar-cutoff calibration and converts each document-level judgment into inspectable evidence records containing local labels, rationales, confidence estimates, and linked spans. Across three domains and four generators, AGENT-XTrust preserves strong binary accuracy while producing inspectable, contestable evidence. In a controlled fixed-stimulus user study, participants assigned to the full AGENT-XTrust system-and-interface package achieved 19.8 and 11.3 points higher decision accuracy than those assigned to the score-only and score-plus-explanation packages, respectively; overtrust on each condition’s detector-wrong cases was 17.8 and 18.3 points lower. These results suggest a broader evaluation target for AI-text detection: not only whether a detector is correct, but whether complete detector-and-evidence packages support reliable human decisions under uncertainty.
